Thanks for the details, and sorry about the dropouts on your Nook speaker. A 2.4 GHz band Nook speaker usually works best in 2.4 GHz band networks, so please make sure that your router is set for 2.4 GHz or switch to 2.4 GHz before trying again. If you still have problems after setting that up, try this: (1) Hold the reset button on the Nook speaker for 10 seconds until the light flashes amber, then hold it for 10 seconds until the light blinks green. (2) Set the Nook speaker up again in 2.4 GHz mode from the app, or switch it off and on again from the router for 30 seconds until the light blinks amber. (3) If it drops again within 24 hours, reply with your router model and our network team will take a look.

Thanks for reporting this. We know about a sync issue in our latest version of the Nook speaker that can cause it to drop or reconnect while connected, and a related bug in our network manager that some people report as a cause. The fix is in version 4.12.3, rolling out now. For now: try turning off band steering in your router app, relasing the Nook speaker once each day, or reset it by holding its button for 10 seconds until you see an amber blink. If it reappears within 24 hours, reply with the start and end times, and we will pull the carrier on the account until the issue goes away.

Thanks for reporting this. We know about a conflict between our band steering software and the Lumen bulb pack that can cause this, and we are working on a fix. In the meantime: (1) Hold the reset button on the Lumen bulb pack for 10 seconds until the light blinks amber, then hold it for 10 more seconds until the light flashes green. (2) Set it up again from the app on the 2.4 GHz network, or switch off band steering in your router app for now. That forces the Lumen bulb pack to reassociate with the network, and usually fixes the connection issue. If it keeps dropping after you turn band steering off, reply with your router model and our network team will take a look.

Thanks for the details, and sorry about the dropouts on your Breeze air purifier. A 2.4 GHz band router usually has two bands: 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz. 5 GHz routers tend to have less interference than 2.4 GHz ones. Please try this: (1) Set both your Breeze air purifier and the router to 2.4 GHz. (2) Hold the reset button on the Breeze air purifier for 10 seconds until the light flashes amber. (3) Pair the device again in the app on 2.4 GHz. If it still drops after 24 hours, reply with your router model and we will escalate to our network team.

Thanks for reporting this. We know about a sync issue in the Lumen bulb pack that can cause these kind of problems, and we are patching the device now. Yes, you can set that up in the app. Open the Ember thermostat, tap Automations, then Add. Choose a trigger (a time, sunrise or sunset, or an event from another device such as the doorbell) and what the Ember thermostat should do in response. Once saved, it runs on the device itself, so your phone doesn't need to be nearby. For voice control, enable the Nook Home skill in Alexa or the Nook Home action in Google Home and the Ember thermostat will appear automatically after you link your account.

Good news: you can do this with the Ember thermostat without any third-party tools. Open the app, tap Home, then Set. Choose a time for the Ember thermostat to start, and it will run on the device itself from then until bedtime. For voice control, enable the Nook Home skill in Alexa or the Nook Home action in Google Home, and the Ember thermostat will appear after you link your account.

That's great to be able to control your Nook speaker from your phone even when you're away! To set it up, sign in to your account, go to Devices, then Add. For voice control, turn on the Nook Home skill in Alexa or the Nook Home action in Google Home, and the Nook speaker appears automatically after you link your account. If you already have two devices, add them both here so they sync automatically.
